title: Microbiota Transfer Therapy alters gut ecosystem and improves gastrointestinal and autism symptoms: an open-label study
description: Open-label clinical trial evaluating Microbiota Transfer Therapy (MTT) effects on gut composition and symptoms in 18 children diagnosed with ASD. Combines antibiotics, bowel cleanse, stomach-acid suppressant, and fecal microbiota transplant. 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V4 region) via Illumina. Alias: Caporaso_Kang_autism. PI: Greg Caporaso (NAU). Also deposited in NCBI SRA under BioProject PRJNA529598. Long-term follow-up showed most GI symptom improvements maintained and autism-related symptoms improved even more two years after treatment.

title: Differences in fecal microbial metabolites and microbiota of children with autism spectrum disorders
description: Case-control study of fecal microbial metabolites and microbiota in children with autism spectrum disorders versus neurotypical children. 44 paired samples. 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Confirmed lower microbial diversity and reduced Prevotella in ASD children. Higher isopropanol and p-cresol in ASD feces; lower GABA concentrations. Published in Anaerobe (2018) by Kang et al. PI: Rosa Krajmalnik-Brown (Arizona State University).

title: American Gut Project
description: Large-scale citizen-science microbiome study (The Microsetta Initiative / American Gut Project). Contains self-reported health metadata including autism diagnosis from participants. 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V4 region) via Illumina. Deidentified data publicly available. Used as reference dataset in multiple ASD microbiome meta-analyses. PI: Rob Knight (UC San Diego).
